nodes.label: Email Client Compatibility Design (table layout, flat hex, no SVG/box-shadow)
nodes.rationale: Table-based layout (no CSS Grid/Flexbox/gap) and flat hex colors instead of color-mix()/rgba() chosen because near-zero email-client support exists for the modern alternatives (per Mailpit's caniemail-backed check): rgba() has real gaps across Outlook Windows 2007-2019, Yahoo, AOL, WEB.DE, GMX, Apple Mail iOS 11, Orange, and Gmail strips the whole style attribute/<style> block on rgba()'s syntax. box-shadow is dropped everywhere since caniemail shows it unsupported/partial across the majority of the digest's real audience. Unicode glyphs (★, ↗, ③) replace inline <svg> since several clients (Outlook Windows, Gmail, Yahoo, AOL) strip unsupported <svg> elements and any fallback content entirely rather than just ignoring them. The @media stacking technique is the standard responsive-email approach (also used by MJML, Foundation for Emails); Outlook desktop's Word engine is an accepted degradation since deep MSO-conditional-comment hackery isn't worth it for a single-operator daily digest.
